newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares hold highs, but wary mood prevails.
newsitem.headline: German shares hold highs, but wary mood prevails.

text.p: German shares were holding at record high levels on Monday afternoon but traders said the market was cautious at the start of a week packed with crucial economic events and meetings.
"The mood on the trading floor was the same as ever," said one dealer of a bourse session which saw the blue-chip DAX index close at a new all-time high of 3,062.29 points.

Volatility on the U.S. markets has repeatedly caused tension on the German stock market in the past two weeks, and the nerves are being compounded this week by key meetings scheduled to take place in the U.S. and Germany.
In afternoon screen trade, the IBIS DAX index was up 23.60 points at 3,061.30 points, almost unchanged from the close of bourse trade, and March DAX futures were up 32 at 3,072 points.
The dollar's firm position at well above 1.64 marks was underpinning broad market gains, particularly on exporters including Daimler-Benz AG and Siemens AG.
But dealers said overall volumes were very weak.

With the Federal Reserve's two-day policy meeting due to start on Tuesday, the Bundesbank council meeting scheduled for Thursday and G7 leaders scheduled to gather in Berlin Saturday, too many variables were in play, dealers noted.

At the same time, there were few serious qualms on the risk of an interest rate hike this week by the U.S., after a raft of economic data showing few inflationary pressures, and the Bundesbank meeting is also viewed as highly unlikely to yield any concrete news.
"I can see us heading to 3,100 (DAX) points now," said one dealer, who added, however, that he thought the market's upside potential beyond that level was limited.
Among the biggest gainers, Siemens AG was up nearly four percent, at 82.85 marks. Dealers saw large foreign orders after its CEO said the group planned to sell non-core businesses.

Metallgesellschaft was up nearly five percent at 34.59 marks after the diversified engineering and trading group reported a surge in profits for 1995/1996 and a 20 percent rise in first-quarter profits.
"The outlook for this year especially has given MG a bit more upward leeway," noted one dealer.
